instructions: Cut the pork belly into chunks about 1 1/2 inches wide. Pat them dry and toss with 1/2 tsp of the salt.

Roughly chop the lemongrass (white parts only), 1 1/2 inches of the galangal, 2 of the shallots and the garlic. Blend them in a food processor or blender with the garam masala, chili powder, turmeric, shrimp paste, the remaining 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water until smooth. Scrape it into a bowl.
Slice the other 2 shallots thin. Cut 2 thin slices from the remaining galangal.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced shallots and the star anise and cook for 3 minutes, until the shallots are soft.
Add the curry paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells toasty and the oil starts to separate.
Add the pork, turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it's coated and starting to brown.

Add the tamarind, sugar, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, galangal slices and 1 3/4 cups water. Scrape up anything stuck to the bottom. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 1 hour, stirring once halfway.

Rinse the rice in a strainer and put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water. Bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Let it sit covered for 5 minutes. Start this when the pork has about 30 minutes to go.
Take the lid off the pork and simmer for 30 minutes, until the pork is very tender and the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vinegar. Slice the cucumbers.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice with the cucumber slices on the side. It keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat it over low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: Cup of Yum leads (5 stars from 2 reviews): a paste of lemongrass, galangal, shallots, garlic, garam masala, turmeric and shrimp paste, fried with star anise, then pork belly braised with tamarind, sugar, dark soy and fish sauce and finished with vinegar. Grantourismo (Ian Kittichai's version, 5 stars from 2 reviews) agrees on the long low simmer and says it tastes better the next day. Chili powder is cut to 1/2 tsp so the pot stays mild, and the cucumber side is Cup of Yum's cooling garnish tip. Fallback, as both pages have fewer than 20 ratings.
